title: Cohomology commutes with filtered colimits on quasi-compact spaces
statement: Let X be a topological space such that the quasi-compact open subsets form a basis and the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact. Let I be a directed set (nonempty, and every two elements have a common upper bound) and (F_i)_{i in I} a system of sheaves of abelian groups on X. For every quasi-compact open U of X and every q>=0, the canonical map colim_i H^q(U,F_i) \to H^q(U,colim_i F_i) is an isomorphism, where H^q(U,-) means the q-th right derived functor R^q Gamma(U,-) on the abelian category of sheaves of abelian groups on the open site of X, as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

proof.text: The compact-open abelian section theorem gives preservation of I-colimits by Gamma(U,-). Its proof works directly with abelian stalk colimits and finite gluing; no equivalence with constant-Z-module sheaves is used.

Induct on n to prove R^n Gamma(U,-) preserves I-colimits. At zero, use Mathlib rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf. For the successor apply the existing general right-derived filtered-colimit successor theorem. Its injective-colimit acyclicity premise is supplied by the compact-open acyclicity theorem.

Use the natural isomorphism between evaluated cohomologyPresheafFunctor and derived sections. Transport the colimit universal property along the isomorphism using IsColimit.mapCoconeEquiv, then nonempty_isColimit_iff_isIso_desc gives exactly the canonical map in the unchanged statement.
